title: Agaricus Muscarius
text: This remedy has a marked action on the nervous system, producing a variety of symptoms, such as twitching, jerking, and trembling. It is especially indicated in cases of chorea and other nervous disorders. It is also useful in skin diseases, such as chilblains, with much itching and burning. There is a general sensitiveness to cold air. Singing, chatting, but does not answer. Delirium. Loquacity. Fearless. Vertigo from sunlight, and on walking. Headache, as if from a nail driven into the head. Icy coldness on the head. Twitching of the eyelids and eyeballs. Double vision. Dimness of vision. Twitching of the facial muscles. Redness and burning of the face. Great appetite. Burning in the stomach. Empty eructations. Distended with gas. Rumbling. Sharp pains in the region of the liver. Diarrhoea of thin, yellow-greenish mucus. Itching and burning of the anus. Frequent desire to urinate. Scanty urine. Shortness of breath on motion. Violent cough, ending in sneezing. Palpitation, with a sensation of oppression in the region of the heart. Stiffness and aching in the back. Sensitiveness of the spine to touch. Twitching and jerking of the muscles of the limbs. Trembling of the hands. Chilblains, with much itching and burning. Chilblains. Itching and burning as if frozen. Eruptions like miliary rash. Worse from cold air and after eating. Better from gentle motion. Compare: Cimicifuga; Calcarea carbonica; Ignatia; Tarentula. Third to thirtieth potency.
